graph_metadata.schema: G = (V, E, X, W) -- V: vulnerability nodes only; E: chaining | co_context | shared_root_cause; X: per-node F_i attributes (T,S,A,L,C,W,E); W: per-edge 'weight' field
graph_metadata.networkx_representation: MultiDiGraph (Multi: a pair may carry edges of several different types; Directed: chaining is directional, co_context/shared_root_cause are symmetric but stored once and treated as undirected via to_undirected() for connectivity checks)
graph_metadata.pyg_directionality_plan: chaining -> single (source,target) edge_index entry; co_context / shared_root_cause -> expanded to both (source,target) and (target,source) entries at PyG conversion time (Phase 4, not yet implemented)

edges.reason: An outdated service version combined with a weak/unencrypted protocol on the same port expands the exploitable surface of that service.
A Content-Security-Policy is a primary mitigation against XSS payload execution; its absence directly increases the impact of the XSS finding.
Missing X-Frame-Options can be combined with XSS for clickjacking-assisted exploitation of the same page.
Without the HttpOnly flag, a successful XSS payload can read the session cookie directly, escalating XSS impact to session hijacking.
Verbose error / stack-trace leakage on the same target helps an attacker refine SQL Injection payloads (classic error-based SQLi workflow).
Successfully authenticating with default/weak credentials grants a valid session that can then be used to probe IDOR-vulnerable endpoints.
Absence of rate limiting on an auth endpoint enables brute-forcing of the same weak/default credentials flagged by the broken-auth finding.
